title: Single molecule magnet behaviour in a {Dy4P2} octahedron

material_class.structural_family: {Ln4P2} phosphonate octahedron; Co3 triangles are countercations

synthesis.procedure: Compound 1 was prepared by reacting Gd(NO3)3·6H2O (0.13 g, 0.30 mmol), [Co3(μ3-O)(O2CtBu)6(py)3]·O2CtBu (1 g, 0.88 mmol), tert-butylphosphonic acid (0.07 g, 0.507 mmol) and pyridine (0.5 mL, 6.20 mmol) in acetonitrile (15 mL) for 7 h to give a brown solution. The solution was filtered and left undisturbed at room temperature for two weeks. Light-brown crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction were collected. The main text states that heating for 7 h was followed by crystallization over three weeks and reports yields of 20–25%.
synthesis.temperature: heated for 7 h, then room temperature
synthesis.time: 7 h reaction, then two weeks standing (main text: three weeks)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction in acetonitrile, filtration, ambient crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered brown solution left untouched at room temperature; light-brown X-ray-quality crystals collected.

properties.summary: χMT is nearly constant from 300 to about 15 K and then falls, consistent with very weak antiferromagnetic coupling. Simultaneous fitting gives J = −0.01 cm−1, comparable to possible Gd(III) zero-field splitting, so a purely single-ion origin cannot be excluded. Magnetization saturates near the value expected for four Gd(III) ions.

measurements.conditions: room temperature; DC field 1 kOe (calcd 31.2 cm^3 K mol^-1 for four Gd(III), g* = 1.99, S = 7/2)

measurements.conditions: saturation above ca. 5 T at 1.8 and 3 K

measurements.conditions: PHI fit of χMT(T) and M(H) to H = −2J(S1·S2 + S2·S3 + S3·S4 + S1·S4) + gμBH Σ Si

synthesis.procedure: Compound 2 was prepared by the same procedure as compound 1, replacing Gd(NO3)3·6H2O with Dy(NO3)3·5H2O (0.30 mmol), together with [Co3(μ3-O)(O2CtBu)6(py)3]·O2CtBu (1 g, 0.88 mmol), tert-butylphosphonic acid (0.07 g, 0.507 mmol) and pyridine (0.5 mL, 6.20 mmol) in acetonitrile (15 mL). The mixture was heated for 7 h, filtered, and left at room temperature to crystallize. The main text reports light-brown crystals after three weeks and yields of 20–25%.
synthesis.temperature: heated for 7 h, then room temperature
synthesis.time: 7 h reaction, then two weeks standing (main text: three weeks)
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reaction in acetonitrile, filtration, ambient crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered solution left at room temperature; light-brown crystals collected.

properties.summary: χMT decreases on cooling from crystal-field depopulation of Dy(III) and then rises slightly, suggesting weak ferromagnetic Dy–Dy interaction. AC susceptibility under an optimal 0.6 kG DC field shows frequency-dependent in-phase and out-of-phase signals below 16 K, characteristic of a single-molecule magnet. Arrhenius analysis gives Ueff = 67 K and τ0 = 2.7 × 10−6 s; Cole–Cole α increases from 0.05 to 0.50 as additional relaxation pathways appear below 11 K. Electrostatic modelling gives nearly collinear magnetic axes (21° deviation).
